title: Al-Sabbah joins General Electric lab in Schenectady
why: AUB-trained engineer, 43 patents made abroad; same route as today's remote engineers.

title: Chiha helps shape liberal, services-based republic (1920s constitution era)
why: Services-and-finance economy has ideological roots; no productive base or shared risk pool.

title: National Pact and independence; Chiha advises Bechara El Khoury
why: Sect-balanced consent from day one still shapes every loss-allocation decision.

title: Youssef Beidas founds Intra Bank
why: A private giant grew to 15% of deposits: single point of failure.

title: Banking Secrecy Law enacted under Chamoun
why: Client names shielded even from judges; reversed only in 2025 under IMF pressure.

title: Fouad Chehab becomes president
why: Rare moment betting on shared institutions over patronage.

title: Musa al-Sadr arrives in Tyre, builds schools and clinics
why: Community networks fill state gaps; template for parallel welfare.

title: Haigazian students form rocket society under Manougian
why: Ambitious innovation began with a college team, not a public research system.

title: IRFED report finds regions far behind Beirut
why: Half of households poor in 1960 (one source): 'golden era' was uneven.

title: Cedar IV rocket reaches about 140 km
why: First Arab suborbital-capable rockets; programme over by 1966 with no institutional home.

title: Banque du Liban begins operating
why: Institution central to Intra's aftermath and to 2019.

title: EDL founded with state electricity monopoly
why: Grid supplied round-the-clock power until 1975: today's generators are a decline, not a default.

title: Intra Bank suspends payments
why: 15% of deposits frozen; who bears the loss when the state declines to cover?

title: Chehabist Sarkis loses presidency by one vote
why: Reform depended on one person; consensus politics reasserted.

title: 13 families reportedly hold 47% of industrial capital, 30% of bank assets
why: Concentrated finance recurs in 2019 loss-sharing fights (advocacy source, unchecked).

title: Civil war begins; state services erode
why: Generators and militia services replace public ones; substitute becomes entrenched.

title: Musa al-Sadr last seen in Libya
why: His community institutions outlived him; the state never replaced them.

title: Pound falls from 3 (1965) to about 500 per dollar
why: First lesson: do not trust the pound; hold dollars.

title: Salibi publishes A House of Many Mansions
why: No shared national story makes shared loss-allocation harder.

title: Taif Agreement signed
why: 1:1 sect parity, no deconfessionalisation timeline: consensus works as veto.

title: Riad Salameh becomes BDL governor
why: One person anchored the country's money for thirty years.

title: Solidere and Horizon 2000 rebuild downtown
why: Reconstruction by a company plus debt (about $18bn by 1998), not public planning.

title: Lira pegged at 1,507.5 per dollar
why: 22 years of peg trust made the 2019 break harder.

title: Rafic Hariri assassinated
why: Political violence shortens every reform window.

title: Circular 331 guarantees 75% of startup equity
why: Startup funding rested on a BDL guarantee, fragile to BDL failure.

title: BDL 'financial engineering' swaps with banks
why: Opaque operations central to later accountability disputes (charges, not convictions).

title: Financial crisis: deposits frozen
why: People move to private dollars, cash, generators, solar.

title: First-ever sovereign default on $1.2bn Eurobond
why: State stops paying; households had already self-insured.

title: Beirut port explosion; Bitar probe begins, later stalls
why: Blocked public accountability deepens the trust deficit.

title: World Bank calls crisis a 'deliberate depression'
why: Outside diagnosis: consensus in defence of a bankrupt system.

title: Banking secrecy amendment adopted, judged insufficient
why: Half-measures under IMF pressure: reform-then-dilute pattern.

title: Official rate devalued 90% to 15,000 per dollar
why: Last official trace of the 1997 peg disappears.

title: Salameh governorship ends; charges abroad and in Lebanon
why: Charges not convictions; institutional trust deficit outlasts him.

title: Judge Bitar resumes port probe, charges 10
why: Accountability moved only after the government changed.

title: Karim Souaid takes office as BDL governor
why: Reform window opens; do institutions outlast personalities?

title: Parliament amends banking secrecy, access back to 2015
why: Reverses 1956 design after 69 years, under IMF pressure.

title: Bank resolution law adopted
why: New restructuring authority; critics call it a missed accountability chance.

title: Cabinet approves financial gap draft law, 13 to 9
why: $80-83bn gap; the loss-allocation decision deferred since 2019; parliament vote unverified.
